beats.care: Lakhs of Indians live and work in Saudi Arabia. Flights from Kerala, Delhi and Mumbai have been cancelled, and fuel prices could stay high.
beats.what: On Saturday, a missile hit King Khalid airport in Riyadh. Saudi officials say 12 people died and 309 were injured.
beats.why: It was the third attack on the airport in a week. Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed the earlier ones as fighting with Saudi Arabia escalates.

cards.body: Saudi aviation authorities say the dead include four Saudis, two Bangladeshis and one person each from the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. No Indian was reported among them. Dammam's airport was also attacked hours later.
An armed group that controls much of Yemen and is backed by Iran. Saudi Arabia leads a coalition fighting them. With the US–Iran war raging, the Houthis have widened attacks to Saudi cities.
cards.title: who are the houthis?

cards.body: India's embassy in Riyadh has asked Indians to stay alert, stay indoors when needed and not share videos of attacks.
cards.caption: 24x7 helpline for Indians in Saudi Arabia

a.body: The Saudi-led coalition says it hit over 130 Houthi targets. President Trump says the US may join strikes.

b.body: More strikes could widen the war, endanger civilians in Yemen and Saudi Arabia, and push oil prices even higher.
b.label: Critics of escalation warn
